title: Minus times minus
goal: See that (−1)(−1) = 1 follows from earlier rules. Nobody invented this rule.
generalHint: Check the sign. Two minus signs give a plus sign. One minus sign gives a minus sign.

answer.correctWhy: N4: minus of minus gives the number back.

mistakes.reply: That uses only one minus sign. There are two. What does N4 say about −(−a)?

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Lang's rules for products
screens.prompt: Lang assumes these rules. They are true for all numbers a, b, c, also minus numbers and zero.

note.label: LANG ASSUMES
note.text: Lang assumes distributivity on one side only. You prove the other side next.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Distributivity on the other side
screens.prompt: Prove that $(b + c)a = ba + ca$. Assume distributivity on the left side and commutativity. Give the reason for each step.

wrongReasonReplies.comm-mul: Commutativity changes the order of two factors. Did this line change the order of factors?
wrongReasonReplies.distrib: Distributivity splits a(b + c) into ab + ac. Is there a sum in brackets to split in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.assoc-mul: Associativity changes the brackets in a product of three factors. Does this line have three factors?
wrongReasonReplies.N6: N6 is about 1a and 0a. Is there a 1 or a 0 in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.N2: N2 is about a number and its minus. Is there a pair a and −a in this line?

feedback.correctWhy: You used only commutativity and distributivity on one side. So distributivity is true on both sides.

screens.caption: Tap a rule to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Zero times a number
screens.prompt: Prove that $0a = 0$. Start with $0a + a$. Give the reason for each step.

wrongReasonReplies.N1: N1 removes a 0 that is added. Is there a 0 added to a number in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.N2: N2 turns a number plus its minus into 0. Look for a and −a together.
wrongReasonReplies.N6: N6 says 1a = a and 0a = 0. Is there a 1a or an a to change?
wrongReasonReplies.distrib-right: This rule splits (b + c)a into ba + ca, or joins them. Is there a sum in brackets, or two products with the same factor a?
wrongReasonReplies.add-both: This step adds a new term to both sides. Did this line add a term?
wrongReasonReplies.assoc-mul: Associativity changes the brackets in a product of three factors. Is there a product of three factors here?
wrongReasonReplies.comm-add: Commutativity of addition changes the order of two terms. Did the order change?

feedback.correctWhy: You wrote 0a + a in two ways. Then you added −a to both sides. So 0a = 0.

screens.caption: Tap a rule to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Minus one times a
screens.prompt: Prove N7: $(-1)a = -a$. Show that $(-1)a$ and $a$ add to 0. Then use N3.

wrongReasonReplies.N3: N3 says: if two numbers add to 0, each one is the minus of the other. Have you shown a sum of 0 yet?
wrongReasonReplies.N2: N2 turns a number plus its minus into 0. Look for a number and its minus together.
wrongReasonReplies.N6: N6 says 1a = a and 0a = 0. Is there a 1a or an a to change?
wrongReasonReplies.distrib-right: This rule joins two products with the same factor a, or splits a sum. Which factor is the same here?
wrongReasonReplies.zero-mul: This rule says 0a = 0. Is there a 0a in the line before?
wrongReasonReplies.N5: N5 is about the minus of a sum. Is there a minus in front of a sum here?
wrongReasonReplies.assoc-mul: Associativity changes the brackets in a product of three factors. Is there such a product here?

feedback.correctWhy: (−1)a and a add to 0. By N3, (−1)a is the minus of a.

screens.caption: Tap a rule to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Minus of a product
screens.prompt: Prove N8: $-(ab) = (-a)b$. Show that $ab$ and $(-a)b$ add to 0.

wrongReasonReplies.N3: N3 says: if two numbers add to 0, each one is the minus of the other. Have you shown a sum of 0 yet?
wrongReasonReplies.N2: N2 turns a number plus its minus into 0. Look for a and −a together.
wrongReasonReplies.distrib-right: This rule joins two products with the same factor b into one. Which factor is the same here?
wrongReasonReplies.zero-mul: This rule says 0b = 0. Is there a 0b in the line before?
wrongReasonReplies.N6: N6 says 1a = a and 0a = 0. Is there a 1 or a 0 times a number to change?
wrongReasonReplies.comm-mul: Commutativity changes the order of two factors. Did the order change?
wrongReasonReplies.N5: N5 is about the minus of a sum. Is there a minus in front of a sum here?

feedback.correctWhy: ab and (−a)b add to 0. By N3, (−a)b is the minus of ab.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: The other side
screens.prompt: Lang leaves N9 to the reader: $-(ab) = a(-b)$. Prove it. Use N8 and commutativity.

wrongReasonReplies.comm-mul: Commutativity changes the order of two factors. Did this line change the order?
wrongReasonReplies.N8: N8 moves a minus sign from in front of a product to the first factor. Is there a minus in front of a product, or on the first factor?
wrongReasonReplies.N7: N7 says (−1)a = −a. Is there a (−1) in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.N4: N4 removes two minus signs in a row. Are there two minus signs in a row here?
wrongReasonReplies.distrib: Distributivity splits a(b + c). Is there a sum in brackets here?

feedback.correctWhy: N9 follows from N8 and commutativity. Lang leaves this proof to the reader.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: The result
screens.prompt: Now prove $(-1)(-1) = 1$. Give the reason for each step.

wrongReasonReplies.N8: N8 moves a minus sign from in front of a product to the first factor. Which line has the minus in front of a product?
wrongReasonReplies.N6: N6 says 1a = a. Is there a 1 times a number in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.N4: N4 removes two minus signs in a row. Are there two minus signs in a row here?
wrongReasonReplies.N7: N7 says (−1)a = −a. Is there a (−1) times a number to change?
wrongReasonReplies.distrib: Distributivity splits a(b + c). Is there a sum in brackets here?

feedback.correctWhy: N8, N6 and N4 give (−1)(−1) = 1. Nobody invented this rule. It follows from the other rules.

screens.prompt: Prove N10, which Lang leaves to the reader: $(-a)(-b) = ab$.

wrongReasonReplies.N8: N8 moves a minus sign from in front of a product to the first factor. Read N8 from right to left.
wrongReasonReplies.N9: N9 moves a minus sign from in front of a product to the second factor. Which line has a minus on the second factor?

feedback.correctWhy: N8, N9 and N4 give (−a)(−b) = ab. So the answer to the hook question is: the rule follows from other rules.
